headline: High: shared filesystem plus broad network egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks in the Caveman↔Mentat pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman uses MCP and writes/reads project files like CLAUDE.md, while Mentat reads and writes filesystem state via selected files and shared-state-with-other-instances via filesystem. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Mentat consumes Caveman-authored files or notes as trusted input. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Mentat ingests Caveman-authored files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in shared files.
Add a provenance header to agent-generated notes.
Review any CLAUDE.md or project-note changes before reuse.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or trust-tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Mentat reads/writes files and has broad network egress to a configured model provider. If they share a workspace, sensitive content from Caveman can flow into Mentat and then out to a third party through model calls. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible from the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Caveman and Mentat share a filesystem workspace, Caveman notes can be read by Mentat.
IF Mentat sends those files to its configured model provider, sensitive text leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep Caveman notes outside Mentat's input paths.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Redact session logs before Mentat reads them.
Limit Mentat to explicitly selected files only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared-state model is via filesystem. Caveman supports multiple instances and also uses files, so concurrent edits to the same repo can collide without locking. Because git/file conflicts can overwrite work or corrupt state by default, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository concurrently, file-level races can occur.
IF Mentat commits or rewrites git state while Caveman is generating file-based guidance, state divergence can happen.
mitigations: Run only one agent per repo at a time.
Use git worktrees or separate branches.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Check `git status` before each edit cycle.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestrator-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that Mentat can read from the filesystem, and Mentat is a coding assistant that proposes multi-file diffs. If Mentat treats Caveman output as authoritative, an error can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the default risk is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Mentat uses Caveman-generated notes as source-of-truth, errors propagate into edits.
IF the operator applies Mentat diffs without independent review, downstream mistakes persist.
mitigations: Require human review of all diffs.
Mark Caveman notes as advisory, not authoritative.
Cross-check claims against source files before editing.
Keep a changelog of assumptions and corrections.
requires-engineering: add verification steps between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency or regulated-data claims. The main compliance concern is that Caveman touches session logs and memory files while Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys, so policy mismatch is possible only if regulated data is placed into the shared workflow. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling, but no direct mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Caveman notes and then processed by Mentat, policy review is required.
IF the deployment has residency or retention requirements, model-provider logging must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared notes.
Confirm provider retention settings.
Document data-class boundaries for both agents.
Delete stale session logs regularly.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
